memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Lord your God delivers it into your hand, put to the sword all the men in it. As for the women, the children, the livestock and everything else in the city, you may take these as plunder for yourselves. And you may use the plunder the Lord your God gives you from your enemies. This is how you are to treat all the cities that are at a distance from you and do not belong to the nations nearby. - Deut 20:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we should not rush past it or soften it. For distant cities that refused peace and chose war, the fighting men were to be defeated, while women, children, and livestock were spared and taken. We must be honest that these are difficult commands from a violent ancient world, and they can trouble us deeply.

To read this rightly, we must hold it in its proper setting. These were specific, limited instructions for Israel at a particular moment in redemptive history, not a timeless command for God's people in every age. Even here, distinctions were made, this was warfare with limits, aimed at cities that had rejected an offer of peace. And notice that God, not Israel's might, is the one who "delivers it into your hand." The outcomes rested in His sovereign purposes.

We can be troubled by such texts and still trust the God behind them, knowing that His full character is revealed most clearly in Jesus. The New Testament reminds us that God spoke in many ways in former times, but has now spoken finally in His Son (Heb 1:1-2). In Christ we see God's heart most clearly, taking judgment upon Himself so that mercy could flow to us. We do not wage war like ancient Israel; our battle is spiritual, and our weapons are not of this world (2 Cor 10:3-4). How does seeing God's final word in Christ help you trust Him even with the hard passages?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you handle the parts of Scripture that trouble you?
2. How does seeing God's heart in Christ help you trust Him?
3. What does it mean that our battle today is spiritual?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when Scripture troubles me, help me trust the God revealed fully in Jesus. Thank You that in Christ I see Your heart most clearly. Amen.
